processors.name: Resolve Kafka topic
processors.comments: matched -> straight to PublishKafka with kafka.topic set. unmatched (a GitHub event type not yet in config/topic-map.properties) routes to the fallback step below rather than being silently dropped

processors.name: Route on HTTP status and rate limit
processors.comments: not_modified (304, ETag hit) is a normal no-op - the next scheduled poll will check again, no rate-limit budget spent. Everything else falls through unmatched to the event-counting step.

processors.name: Poll GitHub Events API
processors.comments: 60s default matches GitHub's X-Poll-Interval; re-tune if a poll response's own X-Poll-Interval header (captured below) says otherwise. If-None-Match/Authorization are only sent when the referenced attribute/parameter is non-empty.

processors.name: Check 300-event ceiling
processors.comments: A poll returning exactly 300 events (the API's documented maximum) is a cheap, reliable signal the 30-day/300-event window may already have truncated real data. unmatched (below 300) goes straight to splitting.

processors.name: Count events in response
processors.comments: Counted before SplitJson runs, on the still-whole response array - the 300-event ceiling check downstream needs the original page size, which is lost once the array is split into one flowfile per event.

processors.name: Log operational warning
processors.comments: Shared sink for: rate-limit-exhausted polls, and RetryFlowFile's retries_exceeded. Visible in NiFi's bulletin board / app log, not silently dropped.

processors.name: Extract event id and type
processors.comments: event.id becomes PublishKafka's message key (kafka-topic-contract.md: same event redelivered lands on the same partition); event.type drives the topic lookup next.

processors.name: Log possible window truncation
processors.comments: Logs and continues - this poll's events still get split and published below, nothing is dropped on this signal alone.

processors.name: Track ETag and rate-limit headers
processors.comments: previous.etag is a plain attribute, not processor state — the loop-back connection to Poll GitHub Events API is what actually carries it forward between scheduled runs, since InvokeHTTP has no stateful capability of its own to read state from a different processor.

processors.name: Log Kafka publish failure
processors.comments: Terminal dead-letter logging for whatever residual failure class Publish to Kafka's Rollback Failure Strategy can't retry its way past (not yet characterised empirically) - ordinary connectivity outages are handled by Rollback instead (queued and retried automatically, see step 15), so this sink is now the exception path not the primary Kafka-failure handler it was in the original design.

processors.name: Log unmatched event type
processors.comments: Visibility so a genuinely new GitHub event type gets noticed and added to config/topic-map.properties, rather than quietly living in the fallback topic indefinitely

processors.name: Retry on connection failure
processors.comments: FR-005: retries InvokeHTTP's Failure/Retry relationships (connection errors, non-2xx) with penalised backoff, distinct from the rate-limit path below. retries_exceeded routes to the shared operational-warning log rather than looping forever.

processors.name: Fallback topic for unmatched type
processors.comments: Must match the default value in config/topic-map.properties (T007) - PropertiesFileLookupService has no native fallback so this value is kept in sync by hand. If T007's default ever changes update this property too.

processors.name: Publish to Kafka
processors.comments: Message key = event.id per kafka-topic-contract.md, so same-event redelivery lands on the same partition. Broker connection lives on the Kafka Connection Service controller service, not this processor directly (NiFi 2.x). Failure Strategy = Rollback: a Kafka outage queues events losslessly on this processor's own incoming connection rather than dropping them — designed for outages up to ~1 hour, see the design-scope note below the wiring table in build-guide.md.

processors.name: Split events array
processors.comments: One flowfile per array element - kafka-topic-contract.md's 'NiFi does not transform or reshape the event before publishing' applies from here on: each split flowfile's content stays the untouched, single-event JSON object.
